correctness.rationale: Given the first n input signs, exactly 2^((n−X_n)/2) independent Bernoulli coefficients contribute. Consequently the conditional parity mean is (1−2p_n)^(2^((n−X_n)/2)). In the filtration revealing the first n input signs but only levels below n, this is the predictable cross-covariance of increment n+1 (increment 1 has cross-covariance 1), with both marginal predictable variances equal to 1. The factor p_n 2^((n−X_n)/2) is 2^((1/2−θ)n−X_n/2−2−δ_n) with 0≤δ_n<1. The strong law off criticality, and the O(n^−1/4) probability of |X_n|≤n^1/4 at criticality, give the respective L¹ approximations by 0, 1 and 1_{X_n>0}. The error in any partial bracket sum on [0,T] is bounded by the whole sum of absolute errors divided by N, which tends to zero in L¹ by Cesàro convergence. The occupation mapping is continuous at Brownian paths with Lebesgue-null zero set; using a step input rather than its interpolation makes a uniform O(N^−1/2) difference to the input path. Bounded jumps and bounded predictable variances give martingale tightness and the martingale and compensated-product identities pass to subsequential limits (uniform integrability on bounded time intervals follows from the bounded-increment fourth-moment bounds after scaling). For the critical limit write M=Y−∫1_{B>0}dB, orthogonal to B with bracket ∫1_{B≤0}ds. On an independent Brownian extension with U put W=M+∫1_{B>0}dU. Then (B,W) has bracket tI, so is standard planar Brownian motion by Lévy's characterization; M=∫1_{B≤0}dW, which proves uniqueness in law and identifies the full limit. The two constant-bracket limits and Lévy's occupation-time law yield the other assertions. Replay is by the displayed parity and bracket calculations and RESULT.md Steps 1–4; the inspected script and its recorded 122-check output corroborate the finite parity identities only and were not executed. The proof gives annealed weak convergence, not quenched convergence or a rate.

value.rationale: Exponentially many active subsets compete with exponentially rare perturbations, and at the threshold fluctuations of the input itself decide whether the motions synchronize. A random, explicitly arcsine-distributed cross-bracket separates this joint law from both independent and coincident Brownian pairs and from a fixed correlated Gaussian limit. The complete annealed classification is useful for this natural family even though its tools are classical.
